findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: FIRST REPEAT: Inspector observed the chemical sanitizing dish machine to initially be dispensing 10 ppm. CORRECTED-the dish machine was observed to be dispensing 50 ppm chlorine after the machine was primed and chemicals were refreshed. Ensure chemical sanitizers used for food contact surfaces are frequently tested to verify proper sanitizing concentration as recommended by the manufacturer's label.
findings.citation_text: 4-501.114(A) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (A) A chlorine solution shall have a minimum temperature based on the concentration and PH of the solution as listed in the chart in 4-501.114 (A). [P]

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
findings.comment: Inspector observed foods in the salad prep cooler to have internal temperatures ranging from 46-57F. CORRECTED- items were moved under time as control. Foods that are not used will be discarded at the end of service (the facility is open for 4 hours at a time). Ensure temperature control for food safety (TCS) foods are used or discarded within 4 hours when out of temperature control (below 41F and above 135F respectively).
findings.citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less. [P]

findings.comment: Inspector observed the salad prep cooler on the line to not be holding temperature. For temperatures within the cooler, reference violation 22. findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition.
findings.comment: Inspector observed multiple house made sauces in the walk in cooler to be held past the seven day date marking period (3/6). CORRECTED- the person in charge (PIC) removed the sauces to be discarded and remade. Ensure all temperature control for food safety (TCS) foods are used to discarded within seven days. The date of preparation, thawing, opening, etc. counts as day one.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.18(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Disposition. (A) A FOOD specified in 3-501.17(A) or (B) shall be discarded if it: (1) Exceeds the temperature and time combination specified in 3-501.17(A), except time that the product is frozen; (2) Is in a container or PACKAGE that does not bear a date or day; or (3) Is inappropriately marked with a date or day that exceeds a temperature and time combination as specified in 3-501.17(A). [P]

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
findings.comment: Inspector observed the triple-door prep cooler on the line to not be holding temperature. All items in prep cooler were probed and voluntarily thrown away. Items probed include: Raw Pork (49.5 F), Cooked Pasta (47.5 F), Raw Steak (47F), Raw Lobster Tail (47F), Raw Salmon (46F), and a house made sauce (47F). PIC stated that all items were stored in the cooler last night, which exceeds the 6 hour time allotment that foods can be between 46-55F. Food is likely out of temperature due to a faulty cooler. Discussed with PIC. PIC has scheduled maintenance on the cooler. Inspector will return 05/20/2025 to re-asses violation.

findings.citation_text: 3-501.13(E) Thawing. Except as specified in (D) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be thawed: (E) REDUCED OXYGEN PACKAGED FISH that bears a label indicating that it is to be kept frozen until time of use shall be removed from the reduced oxygen environment: (1) Prior to its thawing under refrigeration as specified in (A) of this section; or (2) Prior to, or Immediately upon completion of, its thawing using procedures specified in (B) of this section.

findings.title: Allergen awareness training for CFPM
findings.comment:
Inspector observed the active CFPM in the facility to not have an allergen training. The facility has multiple certified CFPMs with allergen trainings. Ensure that the active CFPM in the establishment has an allergen training.

410 ILCS 625/3.07(b). Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Training programs must be accredited by the American National Standards Institute or another reputable accreditation agency under the ASTM International E2659-09 (Standard Practice for Certificate Programs). There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training.

findings.title: Approved thawing methods used
findings.citation_text:
3-501.13 Raw shrimp was observed in a pan of water on the ledge of the kitchen prep sink. Pan was placed under cold running water to finish thawing. Best practices for thawing were discussed. Ensure proper thawing of TCS foods.
TCS food must be thawed: (A) Under refrigeration at 41°F/below; (B) Completely submerged under running water at a water temperature of 70°F/below, with sufficient water velocity to agitate and float off loose particles in an overflow, and for a period of time that does not allow thawed portions of ready-to-eat food to rise above 41°F; (C) As part of a cooking process; or (D) Using any procedure if a portion of frozen ready-to-eat food is thawed and prepared for immediate service in response to an individual consumer's order.

Ensure inside the ice machine is cleaned and sanitized at a frequency to preclude mold buildup.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.citation_text:
3-501.18 Chicken and chicken stock were observed with a date mark of 9/17 in the walk-in cooler. Chorizo in the walk-in cooler also had a label with the number 22 on it, which was assumed to refer to a prep date of 9/22. All three items were discarded during inspection. Ensure prepared, ready to eat foods are used or discarded within 7 days when held under refrigeration.
A food specified in  3-501.17(A) or (B) shall be discarded if it: (1) Exceeds the temperature and time combination specified in  3-501.17(A), except time that the product is frozen; (2) Is in a container or package that does not bear a date or day; or (3) Is inappropriately marked with a date or day that exceeds a temperature and time combination as specified in  3501.17(A).

POST INSPECTION NOTE: If chorizo was made on 9/22 it could have been kept for use through the close of business on 9/28. However, cook on duty at the time of inspection wasn’t sure as to the labeling since all other prepared foods had date marks with the month and date. Product was discarded due to uncertainty.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.citation_text:
4-702.11 Knives were observed soaking in a quat solution at the prep sink in the kitchen. Staff confirmed the knives in question were soiled and soaking prior to washing. While discussing the ware washing process for knives the PIC stated knives are washed and rinsed at the prep sink where soaking was occurring and/or at the 3 part sink. findings.title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control
findings.citation_text:
3-501.15 Noodles cooked this afternoon were observed cooling in a covered pan (~1 gal) in the walk-in cooler. Internal temperature was observed at 69F-80F. Noodles were within the first 2hrs of cooling and were chilled with cold water prior to placing in the covered pan in the walk-in cooler. Best practices were discussed including cooling foods uncovered in small portions, using ice baths, and briefly using freezers when possible to aid in quick chilling. Noodles were moved to freezer to help quick chill. 
Also, trays of cooling chicken were removed from the walk-in cooler, which was not at proper temperature, and placed in pans to quick chill in freezers.
Cooling shall be accomplished in accordance with the following time and temperature criteria: 135F to 70F/below in 2hrs and 70F to 41F/below in additional 4hrs (total cooling time must not exceed 6hrs). One or more of the following methods shall be used to cool foods based on the type of food being cooled: (1) place food in shallow pans; (2) separate food into smaller or thinner portions; (3) use rapid cooling equipment; (4) stir food in a container placed in an ice water bath; (5) use containers that facilitate heat transfer; (6) add ice as an ingredient (when applicable); and/or (7) other effective methods. When placed in cooling or cold holding equipment, food containers in which food is being cooled shall be arranged to provide maximum heat transfer through the container walls and loosely covered, or uncovered if protected from overhead contamination during the cooling period to facilitate heat transfer from the surface of the food.

findings.title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control
findings.citation_text:
4-301.11 Walk-in cooler was holding at 50F and unable to maintain foods at 41F/below (see #22 for details). Call for service was made. The thermostat was also adjusted to a colder setting to allow for a drop in temperature. Staff were advised to limit prep for the evening unless foods will be used by the end of service and/or if the cooler temperature has dropped enough that it will be able to maintain foods at 41F/below. SCDPH Food Program Supervisor will be back tomorrow to check on operational status of the cooler. See general comments for additional information.
Equipment holding cold food shall be sufficient in number and capacity to maintain proper temperature of TCS foods.

findings.title: Food properly labeled; original container
findings.citation_text:
3-302.12 Bulk storage bins for white powders were not labeled as to the contents. Provide and maintain labels on bulk bins of sugar, salt, flour and similar foods that are not easily identifiable.
Except for foods that are readily identifiable/unmistakable, food/ingredients removed from original packaging shall be labeled with common name (cooking oil, flour, herbs, salt, spices, sugar).

findings.title: Washing fruits and vegetables
findings.citation_text:
3-302.15 Cook was observed cutting whole mushrooms for prep. Mushrooms were not washed prior to cutting, and cook stated he did not intend to wash the mushrooms in question. Two boxes were available with one containing whole mushrooms and the other containing commercially processed slices. The sliced mushrooms would appear to be ready to use and not necessarily require washing. However, all produce that is not ready to use, such as whole mushrooms, must be washed prior to use. Whole mushrooms that were cut got washed prior to continuing with prep.
Raw fruits and vegetables shall be thoroughly washed in water to remove soil and other contaminants before being cut, combined with other ingredients, cooked, served, or offered for human consumption in ready-to-eat form.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.citation_text:
6-501.11 & 6-501.12

findings.title: All food employees have food handler training
findings.comment:
410 ILCS 625  Sec. 3.06 Proof of food handler certification was not available for one of the kitchen workers. Ensure all staff that are not certified food managers complete an online food handler certification course within 30 days of hiring, and maintain copies of certifications on-site.
All food handlers, other than someone who has a food manager certification, shall receive or obtain training in basic food handling principles as outlined in Subpart M of the Illinois Food Code.

findings.title: Allergen training as required
findings.comment:
410 ILCS 625 Sec. 3.07 Allergen certifications could not be found for CFMs. Ensure all certified food managers complete a food allergen course to obtain certification by next route inspection.
Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter.

findings.title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting
findings.citation_text:
2-103.11 (O) Employee working in the kitchen did not have a signed reporting agreement on file. Employee has been working at the facility for a few weeks. Owner had employee review and sign a copy of the reporting agreement. Ensure all staff are educated on the employee health policy upon hiring and sign reporting agreements prior to beginning their first shift. Maintain signed copies of reporting agreements for staff.
The person in charge shall ensure that food employees are informed in a verifiable manner of their responsibility to report in accordance with law, to the person in charge, information about their health and activities as they relate to diseases that are transmissible through food, as specified under ¶ 2-201.11(A).

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.citation_text:
2-301.14 Kitchen manager handled a cell phone and continued on to the next task without first washing his hands. Manager washed his hands at the request of inspector.
-Bartender began putting away clean glasses at the bar without first washing hands. Hands were washed after hand soap was provided (see #10 for details).
Food Employees shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms immediately before engaging in food preparation including working with exposed food, clean equipment and utensils, and unwrapped single-service and single-use articles, upon entering the work area, and after after engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.citation_text:
4-501.114 Dish machine final rinse concentration was observed below 50ppm. Test strips used by facility and inspector were registering closer to 10ppm. Call for service was made during inspection. In the meantime, staff were advised they could use the dish machine for the wash and rinse steps and manually sanitize in the 3 part sink.
Dish machine was serviced during inspection. Chemical tubing was in the wrong buckets and not allowing for sanitization. Issue was corrected. Final rinse concentration observed at 50ppm chlorine.
Chemical sanitizer used in sanitizing solution for manual or mechanical warewashing shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions and be maintained at the concentration as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling
Maintain dish machine final rinse concentration no lower than 50ppm and no higher than 200ppm. Use test strips to verify concentration of bleach solutions.

findings.title: Approved thawing methods used
findings.citation_text:
3-501.13 Multiple pans of seafood were thawing at the kitchen prep sink. Cold running water was only in direct contact with one container at a time while other pans of seafood were observed in standing water. All pans that were not directly under cold running water were moved to the walk-in cooler. Best practices for cooling were discussed.
TCS food must be thawed: (A) Under refrigeration at 41°F/below; (B) Completely submerged under running water at a water temperature of 70°F/below, with sufficient water velocity to agitate and float off loose particles in an overflow, and for a period of time that does not allow thawed portions of ready-to-eat food to rise above 41°F; (C) As part of a cooking process; or (D) Using any procedure if a portion of frozen ready-to-eat food is thawed and prepared for immediate service in response to an individual consumer's order.
